BERT4Rec’s random masked reconstruction uses both left and right context, whereas appended-mask next-item inference has no right context. The original method already includes last-item-only masking to reduce this mismatch; endpoint weighting extends an existing mechanism. [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690v2) and [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) support investigating objective alignment, but do not establish that stronger endpoint weighting improves this benchmark.

Suggested diagnostic, inferred from these findings: compare endpoint and interior masked-target cross-entropy, positive-versus-negative margins, and HR@10 using matched targets/candidates where possible. For each historical target, compare bidirectional interior reconstruction against prefix-only prediction ending in a reserved mask; always hide the target. Interpret the difference as right-context benefit, not automatically an optimization defect. Under appended-mask inference, shuffle only nonpadding history tokens, then separately ablate recent versus equally many older interactions. Measure paired changes in target rank, margin and HR@10; preserve left padding, mask position and candidate sets, and read the final nonpadding position. Increased perturbation sensitivity alone does not prove improved recommendation quality.

A [September 2026 temporal-attribution preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27201), covering BERT4Rec among several backbones, reports unreliable raw-attention explanations and stronger faithfulness from gradient-based methods. This favors direct perturbation probes over attention heatmaps. Treat endpoint/interior gaps and recent/older ablation differences as diagnostic evidence; accept supervision weighting only when the fixed macro validation HR@10 improves across the four routed category models.
